intro: Authentication protects your health data: welcome, device pairing, PIN, trusted devices, and recovery. Security should feel calm — not like a quiz you fear failing.
buddyTip: Store recovery information where only you can find it. A trusted device plus a remembered PIN covers most days.
mission: Confirm you know how you sign in on this device and where your recovery path lives — update it if fuzzy.
why: Food, weight, and training data are personal. Sessions, device trust, and PIN exist so casual access stays hard while daily use stays smooth.
Most auth pain is forgotten PINs, new phones, or skipped recovery setup. Fix those once; logging stays uninterrupted.
Invitation-only beta means access is intentional. Follow onboarding prompts rather than inventing workarounds that weaken trust.

points: Device pairing for your account access
Trusted devices for smoother return visits
Recovery paths when a device is lost

misconceptions.truth: It costs a crisis later. Set recovery while calm.

misconceptions.myth: Sharing my PIN with a partner is fine if we share goals.
misconceptions.truth: Prefer separate access patterns. Shared PINs blur responsibility and safety.

how.lead: Treat auth like brushing teeth — brief, regular, non-dramatic.
steps: Complete onboarding prompts without rushing past recovery
Set a PIN you can recall under travel stress
Mark this phone as trusted if offered and it’s yours alone
When you get a new device, pair deliberately; revoke the old one if needed
If locked out, use official recovery — avoid unofficial “reset” folklore
Email hello@kcal.lol only after you’ve tried the in-app recovery path
how.buddyHelps: Auth keeps Buddy’s diary yours. The product assumes privacy is part of coaching trust — not an afterthought.

sections.title: New phone checklist
paras: Install → sign in / pair → confirm PIN → verify a recent Foodiary day syncs → revoke trust on the old device if it’s leaving your control.
steps: Do not factory-reset the old phone until the new one shows your data
Keep recovery material handy during the switch

sections.title: Shared households
paras: Use Spaces for collaboration. Don’t turn one login into a household account — ground truth gets muddy and security weakens.

mistakes.quote: I wrote my PIN in a photo album titled Passwords.
mistakes.why: Too easy to leak. Use a proper password manager or offline sealed note.

mistakes.quote: I ignored recovery because onboarding felt long.
mistakes.why: Recovery is the parachute. Five minutes now prevents a bad week later.

mistakes.quote: I keep reinstalling to “fix” login issues.
mistakes.why: Reinstalls without recovery planning can strand you. Follow Troubleshooting and auth prompts.

encouragement: Secure enough to protect you, simple enough that you still open Home tomorrow — that’s the auth goal. Set it once, then go log lunch.
